data.text/markdown:
SAFT-VRQ Mie: BMCSL vs. Santos hard-sphere reference

Both models treat the hard-sphere reference as non-additive, with the Barker-Henderson diameters ||(d_{ij}||) of the unlike Feynman-Hibbs-Mie potentials, ||(d_{ij} \neq (d_{ii} + d_{jj})/2||):
  • BMCSL + correction (hs_reference="bmcsl", default): additive BMCSL mixture of the like diameters ||(d_{ii}||) plus the correction that is first order in ||(d_{ij} - (d_{ii} + d_{jj})/2||).
  • Santos (hs_reference="santos"): non-additive hard-sphere mixture of Santos et al., as used by Aasen et al., J. Chem. Phys. 152, 074507 (2020), Eqs. (14)-(24). It reproduces the exact second and third virial coefficients of the non-additive hard-sphere mixture.
The dispersion term is identical in both models. Parameters: Aasen et al. (2019) pure (FH1) and Aasen et al. (2020) binary parameters (fitted with the Santos reference). Component 0 is helium in all mixtures.

data.text/markdown:
Cross second virial coefficients ||(B_{12}||)

||(B_{12}||) of the EoS from the mixture virial coefficient, ||(B_{12} = 2 B(x_1 = 1/2) - (B_{11} + B_{22})/2||). The pure-component ||(B_{ii}||) are identical in both models, since the Santos model reduces to Carnahan-Starling (= BMCSL) for pure fluids. Reference: the exact ||(B_{12}||) of the unlike Feynman-Hibbs-Mie (FH1) potential, Aasen et al. (2020), Eq. (50), ||(B_{12} = -2 \pi N_\mathrm{A} \int_0^\infty \left[\exp(-\beta u_{12}(r)) - 1\right] r^2 \mathrm{d}r||), with the same combining rules and binary parameters as in the EoS.

data.text/markdown: At zero density, the two references differ only in the hard-sphere part of ||(B_{12}||): Santos gives the exact ||(\frac{2\pi}{3} N_\mathrm{A} d_{12}^3||), BMCSL + correction its linearization around ||(\bar d_{12} = (d_{11} + d_{22})/2||), ||(\frac{2\pi}{3} N_\mathrm{A} [\bar d_{12}^3 + 3 \bar d_{12}^2 (d_{12} - \bar d_{12})]||). The difference is second order in the non-additivity and therefore small (largest for He/H||(_2||)). The deviation from the exact ||(B_{12}||) of the FH1-Mie potential is dominated by the perturbation (dispersion) terms, not by the hard-sphere reference.

Vapor-liquid equilibria

Bubble-point curves by continuation in ||(x_\mathrm{He}||) up to the mixture critical point or ||(p_\mathrm{max}||).
  • He/H||(_2||): experimental data from the DDB export (examples/uvcs/data/helium_hydrogen_ddb_vle.csv) and GEMC simulations of the FH1-Mie force field (examples/saftvrcs/data/helium_hydrogen_gemc_vle.csv).
  • He/Ne: model comparison only (no data in the repository yet).
